punchline: The Hadza hunter-gatherers get 100 grams of fiber a day or more, while the industrialized world averages about 15.
thirty_sec: The Hadza of Tanzania live on meat, berries, baobab, tubers and honey, and Justin Sonnenburg says they get 100 or more grams of fiber a day, against about 15 for the industrialized world. His lab tracked their gut bacteria through the seasons and saw species come and go with the diet. In mice on low fiber, some species never came back. Whether that harms health is still open.
